newsitem.title: FRANCE: Malt--EU exporters seek modest tonnages at refund.
newsitem.headline: Malt--EU exporters seek modest tonnages at refund.

text.p: European maltsters, facing slow world demand and expecting a rise in the refund applying to malt exports, have failed to bid for large tonnages of EU malt since September 13, industry sources said on Tuesday.
Exporters have applied to export a total of 71,240 tonnes of EU malt at a refund of 32.50 Ecus per tonne, statistics from the European malt industry association Euromalt showed.
The European Commission on September 12 set a refund of 32.50 Ecus for unroasted malt but agreed to revert to a monthly review system for the refunds.
September 30 was the deadline for submitting bids with licences carrying the 32.50 Ecu refund. The licences are valid for September plus a further 11 months.
"There is almost no business lined up. In addition exporters did abstain from placing large bids because they think the existing refund may eventually be raised," one industry source said.
"The market is stuck. There are no large importers in view as most buyers are covered until the end of the year," he added.

Officials familiar with EU policy said the European Commission last Thursday failed to substantially cover part of a large sale to Saudi Arabia with free-market barley to avoid having to raise the malt export refund.
The move was aimed at bringing traders to bid for the existing malt export programme.
Malt exports are usually linked to the last two barley refunds each month. The malt export licences have a long validity of the current month plus a further 11 months.
Last Thursday the EU granted 5,000 tonnes of EU barley at a 27.14 Ecus refund, worth some some $141 per tonne, fob Germany.
Had the Commission covered more sales to the Saudis with export refunds, it would have had to increase the malt refund, member country official explained.
The average fob price of the Saudi deal was $135, meaning the EU would have had to grant a refund of over 35 Ecus.
But malt exporters read these explanations as meaning the EU will eventually raise the malt refund when it finally moves to help cover the Saudi deal.
The malt refund is an average of recent barley refunds, plus a malting barley premium (currently zero), then monthly increments of 1.1 Ecus a month where applicable.
The sum is multiplied by a coefficient of 1.3 to reach a refund for unroasted malt.
"The next time they may give a barley refund of at least 30 Ecus, or rather 32 Ecus. This would yield a malt refund of 41-42 Ecus," one industry source predicted.
But some officials have begun talking privately of applying a "negative" brewing premium which would snatch back part of the malt refund if traders continued to keep the Commission waiting.
Such a step would, however, stir up a row with European maltsters who would see the move as unjustified, the source said.
"All the industry wants is a fair treatment. That is to obtain at least the barley refund multiplied by the 1.3 coefficient," he said.
